target_customer: Drone operators and aviation buyers who need aircraft that take off without runways or heavy vertical lift hardware
problem: Electric aircraft that need vertical lift motors carry extra weight and cost, so a design that reaches flight speed by jumping could cut that burden.
business_model: Hardware aircraft developer, revenue model not stated by any source

founders.name: Matthew Whalley
founders.background_notes: Only founder listed on the YC page. A directory lists him as founder and CEO. No background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: A jumping launch mechanism for an electric aircraft is an unproven aerodynamic and mechanical concept needing flight testing and regulatory approval, hard for a two person team in Johannesburg.

defensibility.rationale: A novel mechanism could be patentable, but no source mentions patents. Rating reflects potential only.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source describes any incumbent acting on this specific idea.

market_need_then: The YC page lists the company in the Drones industry. No source gives demand evidence, customers or spend.

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or brand material was found.

outcome_analysis: Passerine Aircraft joined YC in Summer 2017 to build electric aircraft that reach flight speed by jumping, with a two person team in Johannesburg. The YC directory marks it inactive, but no news, post mortem or announcement explains why or when it stopped, so the cause is not public. Failure factors are left empty because any technical or funding story would be a guess.
notes: Company website is blank in the directory, so there is no site to fetch. Dated competitor search for jumping takeoff electric aircraft returned only generic eVTOL lists, so the competitor list is empty. Funding rests on one database, startuplist.africa: a seed dated 2017-08 with no amount and a 120000 seed dated 2018-03, both led by Y Combinator, with a total of 120000; the 2018 date is after the batch and may be a database artifact. Directory team size 2 conflicts with a database figure of 11 to 50. No outcome source found.
